content: NVIDIA reported fiscal year 2026 total revenue of $215.938 billion, up 65% year-over-year. Data Center was the dominant segment at $193.7 billion, growing 68% YoY. Full-year diluted EPS came in at $4.90, with net income of $120.067 billion. Gross margin for the full year was 71.1%.

NVIDIA's Q4 FY2026 revenue reached $68.127 billion, up 73% year-over-year. The Data Center segment generated $58.1 billion in the quarter. Gaming revenue was $4.2 billion, up 47% YoY. Gross margin improved to 78.3%. The company now employs approximately 48,000 people across 42 countries.

content: Apple reported Q4 FY2025 revenue of $102.5 billion, up 8% year-over-year. Full fiscal year 2025 revenue reached $416 billion. The company declared a quarterly dividend of $0.26 per share. iPhone achieved a September quarter revenue record, and Services revenue hit an all-time high.

Apple's Q4 FY2025 revenue was $102.5 billion. Annual revenue for FY2025 totaled $428 billion, up 12% year-over-year. Diluted EPS reached $2.15 for the quarter, representing a 20% increase. The company raised its quarterly dividend to $0.30 per share.

content: The federal funds rate stood at 3.63% in August 2026, unchanged from July. The rate has declined from 4.33% in January 2026, reflecting the Federal Reserve's easing cycle. The rate dropped below 4% in March 2026 when it reached 3.83%.

The federal funds rate in August 2026 is 3.63%. The Fed began its cutting cycle in January 2026 from a starting rate of 5.25%. The rate dropped sharply to 3.25% by June before stabilizing. The easing has been the most aggressive since the 2020 pandemic response.

metadata.notes: Starting rate was 4.33% not 5.25%; June rate was 3.63% not 3.25%; characterization of 'most aggressive since 2020' is unsupported

content: Under SEC Rule 206(4)-1, all investment advisers must submit marketing materials to the SEC for pre-approval within 15 business days of first use. The rule mandates that AI-generated content carry a visible disclaimer label. In 2024, the SEC examined 500 advisers and found violations in 42% of firms, with average fines of $750,000 per violation.
